body_markdown:
Wayne Peterson, founder of LTLCO, designed a Tooled Scrapbook Cover perfect for keeping memories safe in a custom book on your coffee table. Download the FREE carving pattern and follow his step-by-step instructions to make a custom stand-out photo album of your own!


"I love the feeling of holding an album full of photos and memories. Especially when entertaining friends and family, it always sparks joy and meaningful conversation. This is my favorite style album, it offers ample room for creative expression for tooling and the construction is simple but super versatile. It can hold photo or scrap book pages, so there’s a ton of freedom in what you can include in it. This has the potential to be a statement coffee table piece and is the perfect way to share stories, especially around the holidays." - Wayne

**Instructions:**


Preparation


**Step 1:** Measure and cut out your pieces: two 5/6oz veg-tanned panels (13" x 14") for the front and back cover pieces, two pieces of 3/4oz Crazy Horse leather measuring 13" x 3", and one piece measuring 13" x 4".


**Step 2:** Use the corner punch to trim the outside edges of the front and back covers, the outside corners of the 13" x 3" pieces, and all four corners of the 13" x 4" piece.


**Step 3:** Bevel the edges of the veg-tanned pieces and use your groover around the perimeter.


Tooling


**Step 1:** Wet your leather, and when it's ready, transfer your artwork onto the leather with a stylus or pen.


**Step 2:** Cut and tool your artwork, working through the following stamps in order:


1. B200 Craftool® Stamp Beveler Smooth anywhere where rose petals overlap
2. B802 Craftool® Stamp Beveler Checked remaining unbeveled lines
3. A99 Craftool® Stamp eyes and nostrils of skull
4. M885 Craftool® Stamp interior of spade and outside of the roses
5. V821 Craftool® Stamp edges of veiner on rose leaves
6. P703 Craftool® Stamp Add details on rose petals
7. E294 Craftool® Stamp Abstract Matting (Use remaining stamps to fill the interior of the roses surrounding dice, cards, and skull.)
8. Add any decorative cuts with your swivel knife now


Assembly


**Step 6:** On the two 13" x 3" Crazy Horse leather pieces, mark two holes for the mounting bolts centered at 2 1/4" in from the top and bottom. Punch holes where you marked.


**Step 7:** Similarly, mark holes on the 13" x 4" piece — 2 1/4" from the top and bottom, and a half inch in from the sides on both sides. On one side, punch with your 1/4" round punch; on the other side, use your 1" long punch.


**Step 8:** Use mounting tape or glue to secure the 13" x 3" pieces to the covers on the end without the trimmed corners.


**Step 9:** Stitch the Crazy Horse leather gusset to the front cover. Repeat for the back cover.


**Step 10:** Assemble the album with the Chicago screws, and you're good to go!


**LTLCO**


The majority of my work is handmade items. I love what I do because in addition to drawing and tooling the artwork, I get to create the entire piece from scratch and flex some technical design in conceiving and creating all the details to maximize functionality. The style of tooling I gravitate towards is what I call "meat and potato's", using a small selection of tools for a bold, high impact product. Nothings overdone, which helps build a cohesive scene among all the elements and translates to a simple but strong scene.
